lines.trans: Didn't I tell you? I hate being betrayed more than anything. Three hundred million.
As if I could ever have three hundred million yen.
Then go steal it from Muranishi.
Please wait! I will pay the three hundred million!
Five hundred million. If you're the one paying, it's five hundred million.
Even combining every asset I own, four hundred million is the absolute limit.
Then that leaves one hundred million short.
Mr. Furuya—let this cover the hundred million!
With this, swear you will never have anything to do with us again!
Fair enough, I suppose.
Thanks, Kawada. So—what are the two of us gonna do from here?
All we can do is work.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: お前は俺のことを裏切らないって信じてるぞ。
examples.trans: I trust that you will never betray me.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

examples.text: 言ってなかったか？俺は裏切られるのが何より嫌いなんだ。三億だ。
examples.trans: Didn't I tell you? I hate being betrayed more than anything. Three hundred million.

examples.text: 三億なんて、あるわけねえだろ。
examples.trans: As if I could ever have three hundred million yen.

examples.text: 待ってくださいよ！三億、私が払います。
examples.trans: Please wait! I will pay the three hundred million!

meanings.note: Colloquial quotative/emphatic particle expressing surprise or dismissal.

examples.text: そんなことなんて知らない。
examples.trans: I don't know anything like that.

examples.text: 嘘だなんて信じられない。
examples.trans: I can't believe it's a lie.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

examples.text: いいか、このシーンは機密情報を奪う、この映画一番の見せ場だ！
examples.trans: Listen, this scene where you steal secret intelligence is the biggest highlight of the movie!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.

examples.text: 金さえ払えば、村西さんは釈放される。
examples.trans: As long as we pay the money, Muranishi will be released.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 五億だ。お前が払うなら五億だ。
examples.trans: Five hundred million. If you're the one paying, it's five hundred million.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

examples.text: 全資産合わせても四億がやっとです。
examples.trans: Even combining every asset I own, four hundred million is the absolute limit.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 電波費用が二億五千万、施設の改築費が合わせて二億円。
examples.trans: Broadcast wave fees are 250 million, plus 200 million in facility renovations.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

examples.text: 来月までに保釈金の一億、死ぬ気で集めてこい！
examples.trans: Scrape together the one hundred million yen bail by next month with everything you have!

examples.text: 間に合うわけないよ。一億だぞ。
examples.trans: There is no way we will make it in time. It is a hundred million yen.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: これで金輪際、俺たちには関わらないでください！
examples.trans: With this, swear you will never have anything to do with us again!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

examples.text: これで金輪際、俺たちには関わらないでください！
examples.trans: With this, swear you will never have anything to do with us again!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Always pairs with a negative verb; するしかありません means 'have no choice but to do'.

examples.trans: I only have one thousand yen.
There is no choice but to do it.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
